title: Taco Pizza
shortDescription: Seasoned beef, lettuce, chips on top
subtitle: Seasoned beef, lettuce, chips on top
description: Seasoned beef, lettuce, chips on top. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Brown taco meat
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef over medium-high, breaking into fine crumbles. Drain grease. Stir in taco seasoning and ½ cup water; simmer 5 minutes until thick and glossy. Taste for salt.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 475°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 475°F at least 35 minutes. Warm refried beans gently so they spread — cold beans tear the dough.

steps.title: Stretch and thin bean layer
steps.instruction: Stretch four 12–14 inch rounds. Spread a thin layer of refried beans instead of pizza sauce. Beans are thick; use the back of a spoon in an even smear.

steps.title: Cheese, meat, jalapeños
steps.instruction: Layer mozzarella, cheddar, seasoned beef, and pickled jalapeños. Save lettuce, pico, chips, and sour cream for after the bake — they go limp or soggy if baked.

steps.title: Bake until cheese browns at edges
steps.instruction: Bake 11–14 minutes until cheese is fully melted and crust is crisp. Taco Pizza should cut clean; if beans squeeze out, you spread too thick.

steps.title: Cold toppings and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes. Top with lettuce, pico, crushed chips, and sour cream in stripes. Cut 8 slices per pie and serve immediately — this pie does not hold well on a steam table.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Taco Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Seasoned beef, lettuce, chips on top. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
